subject: paper:meinzer-2014
quote: Adolescents with a lifetime history of ADHD were at significantly higher risk of MDD through early adulthood relative to those with no history of ADHD.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). Establishes the elevated depression risk that co-occurrence rests on, in a large longitudinal school sample.

subject: paper:meinzer-2014
quote: ADHD remained a significant predictor of MDD after controlling for gender, lifetime history of other psychiatric disorders in adolescence, social and academic impairment in adolescence, stress and coping in adolescence, and new onset of other psychiatric disorders through early adulthood (hazard ratio, 1.81; 95% confidence interval, 1.04, 3.06).
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. The prospective effect survives adjustment for a wide set of confounders, moving ADHD from correlate toward antecedent of later depression.

subject: paper:riglin-2021
quote: Our findings suggest that ADHD increases the risk of depression later in life and are consistent with a causal effect of ADHD genetic liability on subsequent major depression.
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Mendelian-randomization plus cohort evidence for a partly causal ADHD to depression pathway — the strongest available support for the consequence reading.

subject: paper:katzman-2017-comorbidity
quote: As many as 80% of adults with ADHD have at least one coexisting psychiatric disorder
rationale: Verbatim from the open-access BMC Psychiatry full text (PMC5567978); the review names mood and anxiety disorders among the most frequent. Reused here for the mood comorbidity; medium because it is an all-comorbidity figure, not depression-specific.
